DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Paragraph Three Takes the Stand

STS-HS9-L4-10001300-HSELA910-MKT-IMR-01 • HS English Grade 9 • Organizing Ideas and Making Connections in Informative Writing
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In a real courtroom a lawyer cannot hand the judge a fact and sit down. She has to say what the fact proves and how it ties to everything the jury already heard. Amina, Farid, and Yulia are running that same test on an essay about three families who traveled a long way to get here. Every paragraph is an exhibit, and every exhibit needs a link that says why it belongs.
Exhibit B is the suitcase. What sentence would you say to connect the suitcase to the main idea of the essay?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amina doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Amina is doing and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
2
What is Farid holding?
Look at the picture. Explain what Farid is holding and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Explain what the teacher is doing and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
4
What kind of place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Explain what kind of place this is and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the board on the easel.
Look at the picture. Explain what is on the big white board and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
6
What is Yulia wearing?
Look at the picture. Explain what Yulia is wearing and justify your answer with evidence you can see. Speak in two or three complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS W.9-10.2 — Write informative and explanatory texts, organizing complex ideas and making connections. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
